target_customer: Immigrants and diaspora in the US and elsewhere sending money to Africa and other emerging markets
problem: Sending money home is slow and costly through banks and legacy transfer firms.
business_model: Remittance fees and foreign exchange spread on transfers
product_category: Cross border remittance and payments app

founders.name: Tope Alabi
founders.background_notes: From ITWeb, March 2021: software engineer who grew up as an immigrant child in the US.

founders.name: John Obirije
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no bio found.

competitors.name: Western Union
competitors.what: Traditional bank and agent based money transfer

competitors.name: TransferWise (Wise)
competitors.what: Online transfers built on the banking system

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile money and bank payout rails across several countries plus compliance are standard but integration heavy.

defensibility.rationale: Licences and payout partnerships help, but remittance is crowded with price driven competitors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were already serving the corridor. Not sourced that any copied or bought Afriex; the company expanded to India, China and Pakistan per Condia.

market_need_then: ITWeb (March 2021) says Afriex grew 20x in 2020 and was processing millions of dollars in payments monthly for thousands of users, in the US and Nigeria and later Ghana, Kenya and Uganda.

branding.name_origin: A blend of Africa and exchange, per the founder and CEOWORLD.
branding.domain_note: Moved from afriexapp.com to afriex.com (permanent redirect); acquisition date not found.

identity.logo: Refreshed version of the earlier logo with new typeface PolySans
identity.visual_style: Brand patterns and illustration system added in a redesign
identity.voice_and_tone: Fairness and access over low fees, per founder interviews

rebrands.why: Company blog says the old visuals were disjointed and inconsistent; no date given.

brand_strength.rationale: A deliberate brand redesign and founder press coverage exist, but no evidence of viral or community pull.

outcome_analysis: Afriex is active. After YC in Summer 2020 it raised a 1.2 million dollar seed in March 2021 and a 10 million dollar Series A in April 2022 and expanded from the US and Nigeria to many corridors including India, China and Pakistan. Remittance rules in Nigeria and a crowded market are risks. No later round, exit or layoffs were found.
notes: Series A lead is given as Sequoia Capital China and Dragonfly Capital by Ripples Nigeria and as Dragonfly alone elsewhere. The 60M valuation comes from a Dealroom profile cited in search results, treated as estimated. Nairametrics also mentions a $1.3M seed 'last May' (2020), unverified. Total raised estimates are 11.3M to 11.4M from aggregators. Competitor sources are dated March 2021, about eight months after the Summer 2020 batch.
